patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Same category, different company size. Choose Ooma only if your buying job matches “SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.” rather than Talkdesk's shape. Choose Talkdesk only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; Elite $165” rather than Ooma's shape. Workflow advantage: Ooma leans business-phone; Talkdesk leans contact-center, customer-messaging. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Ooma is SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.95 — no annual lock-in.; Talkdesk is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; Elite $165; Industry Clouds from $225..
- Company-size focus: Ooma (solo, small-business) vs Talkdesk (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Ooma-leaning business-phone vs Talkdesk-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging.
- Researched limits: Ooma — SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Talkdesk — Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165).

Limitations — Ooma: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus; Talkdesk: Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165); CXA AI (Copilot/Autopilot/Navigator) is typically add-on priced on top of CX Cloud seats.

Poor-fit cases: Ooma is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited · Talkdesk is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Digital and Voice Essentials are channel-siloed — true omnichannel starts at Elite ($165) · Avoid Ooma if you actually need Talkdesk's motion (Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital Essentials from $85/user/mo; Voice $105; )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
